title: Hallucination to Consensus: Multi-Agent LLMs for End-to-End JUnit Test Generation
read_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.02943v7 (25 March 2026; complete 15,083-word article incl. appendices, prompts, experiments and limitations read). Final journal DOI 10.1145/3803418.
datasets: HumanEvalJava: 160 Java classes/methods; correct-source benchmark, with three Pitest mutation variants per SUT for oracle robustness.
LeetCodeJava: 100 sampled Java solutions (50 medium + 50 hard) plus three Pitest mutant variants; problem descriptions supply intended behavior.

Defects4J and SF110 are explicitly excluded because CANDOR currently assumes no user-defined/external dependencies. They are mentioned as future generalization targets/related work, not experiments. BugsInPy and SWT-Bench are not used.
Faulty-code oracle experiments use synthetic PiTest mutants generated from correct HumanEvalJava/LeetCodeJava programs, not historical real bugs.
task: CANDOR is an end-to-end multi-agent Java test generator: (I) initialize a compilable JUnit 5 test; (II) use Planner/Tester/Inspector with JaCoCo coverage feedback to generate high-coverage test prefixes and tentative oracles from source code; (III) derive requirements/specifications from natural-language descriptions, have three DeepSeek R1 reasoning Panelists critique each oracle through Interpreter pipelines, and let a Curator correct it. Measures line/branch coverage, Pitest mutation score and oracle correctness against descriptions/reference behavior on correct and mutant source code.
input_setting: Java source plus natural-language functional description (HumanEval docstrings or LeetCode problem descriptions). During faulty-code tests, the source is artificially mutated; oracle correction uses the external description/specification rather than trusting the faulty implementation. End-to-end evaluation excludes repository dependency complexity.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper Section 4.4 explicitly says code/data are released at `https://github.com/qiqiguana/candor`; repository README identifies CANDOR and the exact paper title, and includes matching HumanEvalJava/Leetcode datasets plus the pipeline. First author author-profile search also lists a LegaTest paper repo, but this separate repository is directly linked by the paper.
source_commit_or_archive: Public GitHub HEAD `157165cc7ac76d72e59ed60d13084d74822c9e2e` (2026-03-18); 1,356 tree entries, ~20.9 MB source/data/tools. Static inspection covered README, root pipeline (`initialize.py`, `generate.py`, `fix_oracle.py`, `main.py`), mutation generator, templates, requirements and complete tree. Includes HumanEvalJava, Leetcode, three Pitest-mutant variants, Maven projects, generated sample outputs and dependency/tool jars. Repository has no root LICENSE/SPDX license. README has setup/path inconsistencies: it documents `agents/...` and `tgen.main`, but pinned tree uses root-level scripts/modules; exact command mapping needs resolving.
license: Paper CC BY 4.0. GitHub repo has no root LICENSE or GitHub license metadata. Some source files/components include separate notices, and dataset is assembled from HumanEval/LeetCode/Doocs repositories with their own terms; do not assume the entire repository/data can be reused under a uniform license.
exact_models: Llama 3.1 70B as the basic generation/interpretation/curation LLM
DeepSeek R1 Llama-distilled 70B as the reasoning Panelist model; three Panelist+Interpreter pipelines
TOGLL CodeParrot-based fine-tuned oracle generator baseline
EvoSuite 1.2.1 and Pitest for prefix/mutation baselines
weights_status: No CANDOR fine-tuned weights; the main method uses local Ollama models `llama3.1:70b` and `deepseek-r1:70b`, with ~48 GB VRAM or dual 48GB workstation setup specified. README/source has model names hard-coded in initializer/generator/oracle fixer, and routes through LangChain ChatOllama. A user's Qwen endpoint is not a drop-in OpenAI-compatible route without adapting model-client configuration; not tested. GPT-3.5 baseline is hosted legacy API; TOGLL requires external fine-tuned CodeParrot weights.
evaluation_route: Full paper read. RQ1: CANDOR reaches ~0.99 line coverage, ~0.95–0.98 branch and ~0.94–0.98 mutation across HumanEvalJava/LeetCode; comparable to EvoSuite on coverage and higher mutation. RQ2: oracle correctness on correct vs synthetic-mutant source; CANDOR ~0.89–0.93 correct-code and ~0.91–0.92 mutant-code, outperforming LLM-Empirical and TOGLL; panel removal costs 6.7–8.6pp oracle accuracy. RQ3 ablations confirm Planner for coverage and panel for oracle accuracy. Public code/data make exact work plausible with Ollama 70B models, but 3× runs, 48GB+ VRAM, Maven/JDK11 and many calls are expensive. No experiments run.
blockers: Not Defects4J/BugsInPy/SWT-Bench and not historical real bugs: faulty inputs are Pitest synthetic mutants on HumanEvalJava/LeetCode. It directly studies oracle correctness under buggy implementation, but not real bug IDs or root-cause classification.
Defects4J is explicitly excluded because the current method does not support user-defined/external dependencies; deployment to Defects4J needs additional retrieval/mocking work.
Source is public and substantive but no repository-level license is present; upstream dataset/source terms must be checked before use.
README run instructions conflict with the pinned tree layout (`agents/`/`tgen.main` vs root-level modules), requiring setup clarification.

Exact model route is local Ollama with hard-coded 70B names; replacing it with user's Qwen/vLLM endpoint requires code/config adaptation and changes the tested model. Hardware requirement is large; runs repeat three times.
Article/source reports a manually constructed LeetCodeJava dataset; LeetCode-source licensing and dataset provenance need care. No public Defects4J reproduction cohort.
concept_fit: Very high concept/oracle fit: the paper explicitly shows code-derived tentative oracles can reinforce bugs, then uses natural-language descriptions, extracted requirements and a panel+Curator process to correct them. Synthetic mutation experiments directly test oracle robustness under faulty source, unlike ordinary coverage-only work. However, it is not a real-world historical bug dataset, lacks root-cause labels, and does not experiment on Defects4J. Strong conceptual candidate for oracle correctness/anti-misguidance; likely a closer concept prior than CATGen or XRepoTest.
recommendation: Promote as a top conceptual oracle prior and a conditional runnable author-code candidate. Its public pipeline/data directly support a future bounded study of description-grounded oracle correction on clean vs synthetic-mutant Java code. Do not call the mutants real bugs and do not treat it as Defects4J/SWT-Bench reproduction. For user's Qwen, evaluate only after adapting the model client and resolving source license/setup; a Qwen run would be an independent variant. Exact paper replication needs local Llama3.1-70B + DeepSeek-R1-70B, 48GB+ GPU, three repeats, and legacy baseline details. No reimplementation/source modification/run performed.
supporting_locations: Paper Sections 3.1–3.3: initializer/validation, coverage-guided Planner/Tester/Inspector, Requirement Engineer, three Panelist+Interpreter pairs and Curator.
Paper Sections 4.1–4.4: explicitly excludes Defects4J/SF110; datasets HumanEvalJava and LeetCodeJava; synthetic PiTest mutants; 3 repeats; local Llama 3.1/DeepSeek R1 models.
Paper Tables 1–2 / Section 5: coverage, mutation, oracle correctness and ablation results on correct/mutant source.
Paper Section 6.2: explicit limitation that Defects4J real bug detection is not evaluated; mutation score is proxy.
Pinned GitHub repo contains complete root pipeline files, 160 HumanEvalJava, 150 LeetCode, mutant variants, Maven/Jacoco/Pitest dependencies, templates and scripts; no root license.
GitHub README provides Ollama setup for Llama3.1:70b / DeepSeek-R1:70b, but run commands reference a different package layout than pinned tree.
